---
title: "Benchmark framework"
---

## Responsibilities

| Layer | Responsibility |
|---|---|
| `sblr` | Statistical models, samplers and public inference APIs |
| `sblrbench` | Simulations, strict alignment, oracle checks, adapters, truth-aware metrics, provenance and reference benchmarks |
| Study repositories | Publication-specific extensions, figures, tables and manuscripts |

## Study flow

```text
data preparation
→ simulation
→ oracle validation
→ method fitting
→ standardized extraction
→ metrics
→ credible-set evaluation
→ reproducible report
```

Prediction studies replace credible-set evaluation with held-out prediction and paired model/representation contrasts. Their allele frequencies, genotype scaling, sparse LD, and summary statistics are learned from training individuals only. Test phenotypes are used only by evaluation metrics.

The ordinary `run_benchmark()` framework executes completed Studies 01–05 and
uses semantic checkpoints for resumable local work. `targets` remains only for
the in-development Study 06 and Study 07 graphs. Published reports never trigger
either execution path: they consume reviewed frozen compact outputs.

## Adding a benchmark

1. Define scientific choices in an ordinary-list `spec.R`.
2. Reuse shared data, simulation, execution, extraction, metric, checkpoint,
   provenance, and reporting functions where their contracts apply.
3. Validate and review compact outputs before promotion into the canonical
   `results/reference/` directory.
4. Add a capsule-only report and catalogue entry, then render and audit the site.

Every completed study separates deterministic tests, explicit execution, and a
reviewed compact reference capsule. Earlier states are preserved by Git history.
Studies 06 and 07 remain development-only.
